signal_hints.spot: Target: name the file, function or page. 'In checkout.ts, the total is wrong.'
signal_hints.proof: Evidence: paste the error, the output or an example. 'It says: Card declined.'
signal_hints.done: Finish line: say what done looks like. 'Done when the tests pass.'
signal_hints.limits: Guardrails: say what to leave alone. 'Don't change the API.'
signal_hints.why: Purpose: say who it's for or what it's part of. 'Our customers need this before tax season.'

tracks.title: The 6 habits
tracks.blurb: Six things a good prompt includes, whoever you hand it to.

lessons.title: Target
lessons.why: When you name the place, nobody has to go hunting for it.

before.text: The date is wrong on the invoice page. Fix it.

after.text: The invoice date from formatDate in dates.ts is a day off. It should show the order date, not the day before.

lessons.template: In <file, function or page>, <what's wrong>. It should <what you want instead>.
tips: Use the real name of the file, the function or the doc.
Wrap exact names in backticks so they stand out.
If it's on a screen, say which page and which button.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: The search in `searchProducts` is slow. It should return in under 200ms.
quiz.explain: It names the exact function, so there's no hunt and no guess.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: The welcome email should use the customer's first name. Don't change the subject line.
quiz.explain: Which welcome email? Name the file or template it lives in.

lessons.title: Evidence
lessons.why: The exact error or output says more than any description of it.

before.text: The checkout page is broken. Can you fix it?

after.text: Checkout fails when I click Pay. The console says: TypeError: total is undefined. Please fix it in checkout.ts.

lessons.template: When I <do this>, I get <the exact error or output>. Here it is: <paste it>.
tips: Paste the exact error. Don't retell it from memory.
Show what you got and what you expected.
One real example beats a paragraph of description.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Expected the order date, but every row in the CSV export shows 1970-01-01.
The CSV export gives weird dates.
quiz.explain: It shows what you saw and what you wanted, so the gap is plain.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: In report.py, the monthly totals look off. They should match the bank statement.
quiz.explain: Look off how? Show one total you got and the one you expected.

lessons.title: Finish line
lessons.why: If you don't say what finished looks like, you get someone else's idea of it.

before.text: Write an email to the team about the office move.

after.text: Write a short email to my team about the office move. It should list the new address and the move date, in under 100 words.

lessons.template: <the task>. Done when <how you'll check it>.
tips: Say how you'll check it: the tests pass, it fits on one page, it matches the old output.
Name the shape you want: a table, a list, three bullet points.
If there's a length, say it.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Update the Q3 report so the summary fits on one page, as a bulleted list.
quiz.explain: You'll know it's done when it fits on one page as a list.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: Rename getUser to fetchUser because the old name confuses new hires. Don't touch the tests.
quiz.explain: How will you know it worked? Say what to check, like the build passing.

lessons.title: Guardrails
lessons.why: Guardrails stop the extra changes you'd have to find and undo later.

before.text: Clean up the styles on the pricing page.

after.text: Clean up the styles in pricing.css. Only change spacing and colors. Keep the layout as it is.

lessons.template: <the task>. Only change <what's in scope>. Don't touch <what's off limits>.
tips: Say what's off limits: other files, the public API, the wording.
Name the scope: only this page, only this function.
A guardrail is cheaper than a cleanup.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Tidy up checkout.ts. Don't rename anything and don't add new packages.
quiz.explain: Same task, but now the names and the packages are safe.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: In about.html, fix the typo in the first paragraph because the founders spotted it. It should say 'founded in 2019'.
quiz.explain: Nothing says to leave the rest of the page alone, so expect a few bonus edits.

lessons.title: Purpose
lessons.why: The goal answers all the small questions you didn't think to spell out.

after.text: Make the signup form shorter. Our customers give up at the phone number step. Keep the email field.

lessons.template: <the task>. The goal is <what this is for, or who it's for>.
tips: Share the purpose, not just the task.
Say who it's for: your team, a customer, a demo.
One sentence of purpose is plenty.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Cache the price list because the supplier lets us call them once a minute.
quiz.explain: Knowing the reason tells you how long the cache can last.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: Add a dark mode toggle to settings.tsx. Don't change the default theme. Done when it remembers the choice.
quiz.explain: Who asked for it, and what for? That shapes every small choice.

lessons.title: Context
lessons.why: What you already know saves the first wrong turn, and the second.

before.text: The search page is slow. Make it faster.

after.text: The search in searchProducts.ts is slow once a filter is on. I already tried adding an index and it changed nothing. It should return in under 200ms.

lessons.template: <the task>. I already know <what you found>. I already tried <what didn't work>.
tips: Say what you already tried and ruled out, and what happened, so nobody checks it twice.
Share facts the code can't show: what changed, and when it started.
Say facts about your setup and taste: “it's a Squarespace site”, “we use Tailwind”.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Fix the crash on empty carts.
Fix the crash in `cart.ts` on empty carts. It started after we added coupons, and it only happens when one is applied.
quiz.explain: It says where to look and what changed, so the first guess is a good one.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: The nightly import in `import.py` fails. I already checked the file format and it's fine, so look at the dates.
quiz.explain: It rules out the file format, so nobody spends time checking it again.

tracks.title: Follow up less
tracks.blurb: Get it right in the first message, so you don't have to keep following up.

lessons.title: Say it all up front
lessons.why: Every 'oh, and also' sends the work around again. Put it in the first message.

before.text: Add a CSV export to the orders page.

after.text: Add a CSV export to the orders page. Include the date, customer and total. Make sure it works with 10,000 rows. Don't change the page layout.

lessons.template: <the task>. It needs <every must-have>. Don't <what to avoid>.
tips: Before you send, ask yourself: what would I add next?
List every must-have in the first message.
If you catch yourself typing 'also', it belonged in the prompt.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Add a search box to the help page.
Add a search box to help.html. It should search titles only, and it must work on phones.
quiz.explain: The phone part is said up front, not sent later as an 'also'.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: Add a CSV export to orders.ts. It should include tax. Don't change the table.
quiz.explain: Who needs the export, and for what? That's where the next 'also' hides.

lessons.title: Say exactly what you mean
lessons.why: Words like 'it', 'the header' or 'clean it up' can mean three things. Pick one, and you won't need 'I meant'.

after.text: Update the page header in header.tsx, not the email header. Change the title to 'Spring sale' and leave the logo alone.

lessons.template: In <exact place>, change <exact thing> to <exact result>. Not <the thing it could be mixed up with>.
tips: Swap 'it' and 'this' for the real name.
If two things share a name, say which one.
Say 'not the X' when there's an easy wrong guess.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Make the Save button on the settings page 48px tall. Leave the Cancel button alone.
quiz.explain: Which button, how big, and which one to skip. Nothing left to guess.

lessons.title: Plan big tasks first
lessons.why: A plan you can read in a minute corrections a wrong turn before hours of work get thrown away.

before.text: Move the app from the old payment system to the new one.

after.text: We need to move checkout to the new payment system. Before any code, give me the plan as a list. Don't start until I say go.

lessons.template: <the big task>. Before you start, give me the plan as a list. Wait for my OK before you change anything.
tips: Ask for a plan when the work touches many files or will take a while.
Read the plan. Fix it there, while changes are cheap.
Say 'wait for my OK' so the work doesn't start early.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Rewrite the billing module. First give me the plan as a list, and don't change any files until I approve it.
quiz.explain: You get to check the route before anyone starts driving.

quiz.question: What's this prompt missing?
quiz.prompt: Split utils.ts into smaller files. Give me the plan as a list first. Don't move anything yet.
quiz.explain: Smaller for what? Faster builds and easier reviews lead to different plans.

lessons.title: Let it ask first
lessons.why: When the task is fuzzy, even to you, a few questions up front beat a wrong first draft.

before.text: Write a welcome email for new customers.

after.text: Write a welcome email for new customers. The goal is a second order from each of them. Keep it under 120 words. If anything is unclear, ask me questions before you start.

lessons.template: <the task>. The goal is <the goal>. If anything is unclear, ask me questions before you start.
tips: Use it when you can't picture the result yet.
Answer the questions, then let the work start.
Ask for a few questions at a time, not twenty.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Plan the offsite for my team of 12. Ask me questions first if anything is unclear. Don't book anything yet.
quiz.explain: It gives the who, a safe limit, and room to ask before guessing.

tracks.title: Correct more
tracks.blurb: Check the work before you trust it.

lessons.title: Ask for proof
lessons.why: A confident answer isn't a checked one. Asking where it came from takes ten seconds.

before.text: Update the refund flow to use the retry helper.

after.text: Update the refund flow in refunds.ts to use retryPayment. Before you change it, show me where retryPayment is defined. Don't write a new helper.

lessons.template: <the task>. Before you rely on <the name or fact>, show me where it's defined.
tips: Ask 'where is that defined?' for any name you don't recognize.
Ask for the source: the file, the line, the page of the doc.
If it can't point to it, treat it as a guess.

quiz.question: The answer uses a `maxRetries` setting you've never seen. What's your next step?
options: Ask where it's defined, then look at that spot.
quiz.explain: A name you can't find is a guess until you see it in the code.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Use the parseCsv helper for the import.
Use the parseCsv helper for the import. First show me the file where parseCsv is defined, and don't write a new one.
quiz.explain: It asks to see the helper before trusting that it exists.

lessons.title: Run it before you trust it
lessons.why: Work that looks right and work that works are not the same thing. Running it is how you know.

after.text: Fix the off-by-one date bug in formatDate. Add a test for the last day of the month, and run it before you say it's fixed.

lessons.template: <the task>. Add a test for <the case that broke>. Run it and show me the result.
tips: Ask for a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
Try it yourself: click the button, open the file, read the email out loud.
'Should work' is not the same as 'works'.

quiz.question: You're told the bug is fixed. What do you do first?
options: Run the tests and try the broken case yourself.
quiz.explain: Being sure isn't proof. A passing test and your own try are.

quiz.question: Which prompt is more specific?
options: Fix the login timeout in session.ts. Make sure the tests pass, and add one for an expired session.
quiz.explain: It says where, and how you'll both know it works.

lessons.title: Watch for confident guesses
lessons.why: A wrong answer can sound just as sure as a right one. Learn the tells.

after.text: Make the upload in upload.ts faster. Only use code that's already in the project, and show me the before and after times.

lessons.template: <the task>. Only use <functions or sources> that already exist. Show me <the test, output or source> for each claim.
tips: Watch for names you've never seen. Search for them.
'Fixed!' with no test or output is a claim, not proof.
Be extra careful with exact numbers, dates and quotes. Check them at the source.

quiz.question: Which of these is the biggest red flag?
options: It calls a function you can't find anywhere.
It asks you a question first.
quiz.explain: A made-up name looks just like a real one. Search before you trust it.

quiz.question: The reply says 'Fixed, it works now' and shows nothing else. What's the best answer?
options: Show me the test run or the output.
quiz.explain: Ask for the evidence. If it's real, it takes a second to show.
